trickyParts: protocol.js disconnect() is reached only from the heartbeat's stale path and handleAuthError; reconnect() (client-initiated, live connection) keeps transport.disconnect() and its flush. transport.close() runs _closed(undefined, false): no flush, destroys the socket, resolves closed(), and protocol.js then runs disconnected(lastError) and the redial as before.

The pausing freeze makes stallNext connections the only ones that still read; they model a server that accepts and never answers, so the client's close of a hung redial is observable (closedAt records the FIN or close, since the proxy runs allowHalfOpen).

Editing a file under node_modules/.bun for a negative control writes through to bun's install cache: bun 1.4.4 hardlinks each patched package from the cache entry nats@2.29.3@@@1_patch_hash=<hash>, so a reinstall hands back the edited copy. A control must delete that cache entry (or copy the file aside first) before it restores with bun install.
